title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 5.60
exact_target: Does a simultaneous zero-free Hadamard-convolution condition survive decreasing a real kernel exponent by one?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $\mathbb D=\{z:|z|<1\}$. For analytic functions
$u(z)=\sum_{k\geq0}u_kz^k$ and $v(z)=\sum_{k\geq0}v_kz^k$,
their Hadamard convolution is the coefficientwise product
$(u*v)(z)=\sum_{k\geq0}u_kv_kz^k$, which is analytic on
$\mathbb D$.
For real $\alpha,\beta\geq1$ and $|x|=1$, put
\[
 K_{\alpha,\beta,x}(z)=
       \frac{(1+xz)^\alpha}{(1-z)^\beta}.
\]
Both powers use the analytic logarithms on the disk normalized
to have value zero at $z=0$, so the kernel has constant term $1$.

Suppose that $\phi$ is analytic on $\mathbb D$ and that
\[
 (\phi*K_{\alpha,\beta,x})(z)\ne0
 \quad\text{for every }|x|=1\text{ and every }z\in\mathbb D.
\]
Must the same simultaneous zero-free property hold after lowering
the numerator exponent by one, that is,
$(\phi*K_{\alpha-1,\beta,x})(z)\ne0$ for every such $x,z$?
There is no boundedness, univalence, or coefficient-sign
assumption on $\phi$; the hypothesis itself implies
$\phi(0)\ne0$.

The implication is required uniformly over all analytic $\phi$
and all real $\beta\geq1$. The source records the implication for
integer $\alpha$, so the remaining target is the noninteger
range $\alpha>1$. A counterexample must satisfy the first
zero-free condition for every boundary parameter $x$, while
the lowered kernel fails for at least one parameter and one
point of the open disk.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does a simultaneous zero-free Hadamard-convolution condition survive decreasing a real kernel exponent by one?
